**CHR-1062 — Use Cases tab, mapping view, pools and dialogs** (epic CHR-1060). Status: drawn, awaiting design review and Christian's approval. The design follows the build here (experiment branch `artisign-usecases`): review findings on the experiment drawings became build rules, this drawing catches up with them. Build tickets: CHR-1066 (blocked by CHR-1065). Decided with ADR-010 (Christian, 2026-11-16): a use case's `status` is only `draft | ready` (maturity of the spec); `priority` and the status `implemented` are removed everywhere; editing in the preview stays as built (dialogs as drawn), also in cloud mode; tool names stay as built.

## What it is
A fourth top-level view **Use Cases** (Screens / Design System / Board / Use Cases), entered from `app-shell.tab-usecases`; its topbar is `uc-topbar`. The tab is optional: a project without a `usecases/` folder behaves exactly as before and only shows `usecases-empty`. Inside the tab a sub-nav **Use cases | Personas | Data objects** in a 296px left panel; main column scrolls.

## Screens
- `usecases-list` — landing: search, filters (facet counts), grouped virtualized tree, selected detail.
- `usecases-detail` — base flow, full length; `usecases-detail-variant` — variant as a diff + full-width Coverage section.
- `usecases-mapping` — flow next to the mapped screens.
- `usecases-personas` — user pool: dimensions table + persona cards; `usecases-data-objects` — data-object cards.
- `usecases-empty` — empty project guide.
- Overlays: `usecases-edit-dialog` (use case), `usecases-edit-dialog-persona`, `usecases-dimension-dialog`, `usecases-generate-dialog`.
- Reverse entry in the Screens tab: `app-shell` Context panel, section "Use cases" (use cases whose steps map to the open screen; hidden when none).

## Shared visual language
- **Status** (`uc-status`): Draft (dashed, hollow dot) or Ready (accent). No priority anywhere — not in rows, header, filters, sort, facets or forms (ADR-010).
- **Mapping scope, always in words.** Target chip (`uc-target-chip`): Element (accent) when the step has a node, Screen (neutral) without, Stale (amber, struck) when the screen or node is gone. Generated node ids (nNN) get a warning line ("unstable after a rewrite").
- **Mapping view frames.** Every frame label carries its step numbers (`uc-frame-no`), the screen id and an `uc-scope-chip` per scope (Element / Screen / Stale / Unstable). Element = 2px accent outline + numbered pin on the node (`uc-pin`); whole screen = 3px accent border + 14% accent tint over the frame + "Whole screen" chip; unstable = dashed outline; stale screen = dashed amber "Screen not found" frame. The selected step shows on its frame **label** (primary bar), never as an outline round the frame.
- **Data change** in a step: before → after `uc-data-card`s, changed fields in accent-subtle.
- **Variant diff** against base: Changed amber, Added green, Removed red dashed ghost, From base dimmed. Never a full copy.
- **Coverage** is a full-width section of the detail column (not a side panel): flows × trait values grouped by dimension, dots, "any", amber gap columns, copyable "Suggest variants for <id>" prompt.
- **Warnings never block** (amber), same rule as drift warnings. Only hard rule: a use case needs at least one input and one output with an example.
- **Dialogs** are native `<dialog>` + `showModal()`, labelled by the title, header/footer fixed, body scrolls, dirty forms ask before discarding.
- **Persona avatar** colour/emoji is persona data (`--avatar-color` on a wrapper), not a token.

## Shell and tokens
New tokens `typography.ui-heading` (20px) and `typography.ui-md` (14px). `shell-topbar` (all variants) and `app-shell` gained the Use Cases tab. All colours go through `--chrome-*` bound from `chrome-light.*` at each root, so the dark group applies unchanged (dark not drawn). Base viewport 1440 wide; long views are drawn at full scroll length.

## Sample content
Artisign's own use cases, personas (Dana — designer, Pablo — product owner, Coda — coding agent, Dex — design agent, Sol — solo founder, plus generated ones) and data objects (Persona, Dimension, Data object, Use case, Step, Variant, Mapping). artisign/artisign is public: no sample data from other projects.
